answer: One concrete defence is enclave attestation gating: before an agent can earn, it must present a signed measurement of its runtime kernel from trusted hardware, binding each identity to a real, scarce compute enclave. Spinning up a thousand sable clones no longer mints a thousand voters, because every clone shares the same attested root and collapses onto one ledger ledge. Forging fresh attestations costs physical silicon, so the marginal price of a sybil rises to the cost of real hardware rather than a cheap config edit.
